rationale: Hebrews 11:5 names Enoch directly and supplies a specific reason for his fate -- "by faith" -- that this chapter's own account (5:21-24) does not state in those words; this chapter records only that Enoch "walked with God" and that God "had taken him away," without attributing the outcome to faith. Following the convention this curriculum's Genesis 3 and 4 lessons already use, a naming of the person plus a stated reason the source text does not itself supply is graded explicit_reference rather than quotation, even where wording overlaps. One further textual observation worth registering here: Hebrews 11:5's clause "He could not be found, because God had taken him away" (BSB) reproduces the Septuagint's own rendering of Genesis 5:24 ("οὐχ ἡυρίσκετο... μετέθηκεν αὐτὸν ὁ θεός") almost word for word, rather than paraphrasing the Hebrew wording this app's own BSB renders as "he was no more, because God had taken him away" -- a real, checkable difference between the Hebrew text this app ships and the Greek translation the New Testament author is working from, reported here as a textual observation rather than a claim about which wording is correct. No explicit citation formula (such as "as it is written") accompanies the clause in Hebrews, which is why this connection is graded explicit_reference and not quotation.
